answer: The nadir detector writes to raven, and terrace makes public every merge. Submissions that land within 288 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. A farm scripting its whole army of identities fires them together, as a result the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 188 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
